clue.text: Chance of work having left college totally discontented

parts.note: op. is the short form of opus, a musical work
port is the left side of a ship
uni is short for university, a college

indicators.note: with its contents gone, only the outside letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A student drops out of college in disgust, and that becomes their big break for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' strips TOTALLY to its outer letters, TY.
explanation.definitionFit: An opportunity is a favourable chance or opening to do something.

clue.text: Group of soldiers playing polo at battalion's base

indicators.note: the letters of polo at are played about with, i.e. rearranged
in a down entry the base of a word is its bottom, i.e. its final letter

explanation.surface: Soldiers in a battalion relax with a game of polo back at their base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges POLO AT into PLATOO; 'base' takes the last letter of battalion's, N.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a small military unit, a subdivision of a company of soldiers.

clue.text: Upset about argument involving brothers essentially

indicators.note: the first pieces take in the next one, which goes between them

parts.note: over can mean about, as in fighting over something
a row is a noisy quarrel

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central part, so the middle letters are taken

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed by a family quarrel at the heart of which are some brothers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads like distress but is the verb to topple; 'involving' sets the core of brothers between the two synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset a government or an object is to topple it, which is an overthrow.

clue.text: Pulse broth to be stirred

indicators.note: stirring mixes a liquid up, so the letters of broth are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction: lentils or other pulses go in the broth, which then needs stirring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a lentil going in the broth; it is the beat of the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular beat, the same as a pulse.

clue.text: Old Testament book characters

definitions.meaning: The fourth book of the Old Testament
numerals are characters used in writing, as letters are

explanation.surface: A bare pairing of a book of the Bible with the people in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers names a book of Moses; numbers are also written symbols, i.e. characters.

clue.text: Oddly unseen, Brummie punches head of Parisian six-footer

indicators.note: a punch goes into a target, so these letters go into the head

parts.note: tete is the French word for head, so a Parisian's head

indicators.note: with the odd-numbered letters out of sight, only the second, fourth and sixth letters show

explanation.surface: A man from Birmingham, unnoticed, lands a blow on a Frenchman's head.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brummie is someone from Birmingham; 'Oddly unseen' keeps only the even letters of that word, and 'punches' drives them into the French head.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects have six legs, so a termite is jokingly a creature with six feet.

clue.text: State gift Anna has ordered

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Anna has ordered a present, though the State in question is left vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Afghanistan is a country, and a country is a state.

clue.text: Verbose master, cross about student interrupting originally

indicators.note: the first pieces go around the next ones

parts.note: a pro is an expert, someone who has mastered a skill
X is the shape of a cross
L is the learner, a student driver's plate

indicators.note: taking a word at its origin means its first letter

explanation.surface: A long-winded teacher gets cross when a student keeps interrupting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L and I (first letter of interrupting) between PRO and X.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolix speech or writing uses too many words, so it is wordy.

clue.text: Gold object found by female in desert

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
sake means purpose or object, as in for the sake of

explanation.surface: A woman finds a golden treasure lying in the sand of a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like the sandy place; it is the verb, to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: To forsake someone is to abandon them, which is to desert them.

clue.text: Comment, on record

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a mark is a recorded score, as in marking down a result

explanation.surface: A remark made for the record, as an official comment.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is something said in passing, a comment.

clue.text: Keep on kissing amorously side by side

definitions.meaning: to neck is to kiss amorously
level, as in a race where the leaders are inseparable

explanation.surface: Lovers who can't stop kissing sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Neck and neck is the idiom for two competitors level, alongside each other in a race.

clue.text: Reportedly sank golf putt last

indicators.note: what is reported is heard said aloud, so the answer sounds like the phrase

parts.note: a golfer who sinks the final putt has holed out

explanation.surface: A golfer sinks the putt on the final hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like the final putt; it is the verb, to endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold out is to keep going or endure, which is to last.

clue.text: Hairstyle from which queen rarely departs?

definitions.meaning: a tall dome-shaped hairdo popular in the 1960s
the queen bee stays in the hive, leaving it very seldom

explanation.surface: A wry remark about a monarch who never leaves her hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: The beehive hairdo is named after the dome shape of a straw bee skep, home of the queen bee.

clue.text: Small number, around nine, meeting new US president

indicators.note: the first piece is placed around the second

parts.note: No. is the short form of number
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Arithmetic around nine is somehow connected with a new American president.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Nixon was the 37th president of the United States.

clue.text: No sign of hesitation chopping up supermarket beef

indicators.note: says that these letters are missing from what is cut up
the letters of supermarket are chopped and rearranged

parts.note: er is the sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: A butcher at the supermarket chops beef without a moment's hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopping up' rearranges SUPERMARKET, and 'No' takes ER out of it, leaving the letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rump steak is a cut of beef from the hindquarters.

clue.text: Element amusing me getting drunk

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone finds their own drunkenness amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesium is a chemical element, a light silvery metal.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing caught by friend wearing stolen goods

indicators.note: the loot is worn around the pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: swag is a thief's loot
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an ally is a friend on your side

explanation.surface: A thief is caught by a friend while wearing stolen clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallywag is a rascal or rogue, a worthless person.

clue.text: American stylist ultimately cuts facial hair for diplomat

indicators.note: the letter cuts into the moustache, going inside it

parts.note: tache is short for moustache

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of a word is its last one

explanation.surface: An American barber finally trims a diplomat's moustache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes T, the last letter of stylist; 'cuts' puts it into TACHE after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An attache is a junior diplomat on an ambassador's staff.

clue.text: They tweet seconds after upsetting football result?

indicators.note: this letter is placed after the turned piece
in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: ten-nil is a lopsided football score

explanation.surface: Tweets fire off seconds after a shock football result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns TENNIL into LINNET. 'They tweet' suggests social media posts; it means songbirds.
explanation.definitionFit: Linnets are small finches, songbirds that chirp, i.e. tweet.

clue.text: Many times moderate leader is ignored

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to soften is to moderate or tone down

explanation.surface: A moderate party leader keeps being ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader is ignored' drops S from SOFTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means frequently, on many occasions.

clue.text: Love times working with Scotsman, Magdalen graduate possibly

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
X is the multiplication sign
on means operating, working
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scot works with a loved one alongside a graduate of Magdalen.
explanation.definitionFit: Magdalen is an Oxford college, and an Oxonian is a member or graduate of Oxford University; possibly marks the example.

clue.text: Age when son abandons craving privacy at last

indicators.note: the son leaves the craving, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a thirst is a strong craving

indicators.note: taking a word at its end means its final letter

explanation.surface: At some age a son gives up his craving for privacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' drops S from THIRST; 'at last' adds Y from privacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirty is an age in years, a milestone birthday.

clue.text: Criminal not many go to stop, perhaps

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Few criminals go so far as to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' says the pair is just one example of opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word of opposite meaning, as go is the opposite of stop.

clue.text: Major's 22 and popular amongst male soldiers

definitions.note: 22 is the answer ANTONYM, so this means the opposite of major; the definition is an adjective

indicators.note: the popular piece goes amongst the others, inside them

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: An army major is popular among the male soldiers he commands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' looks like the officer; it is the adjective, whose opposite (22, antonym) is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor is the opposite of major, smaller or less important.

clue.text: From Hanoi to Mekong, travelling west, there's excitement

indicators.note: in an across clue west is leftwards, so the letters are read right to left
the answer is taken out of the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: A trip west from Hanoi to the Mekong river is a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' and 'travelling west' give the answer backwards inside hanOI TO MEkong.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotion is a strong feeling, and excitement is one such feeling.

clue.text: Vet observed tackling case of canker

indicators.note: the first piece takes on the second, holding it inside

parts.note: seen means observed

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A vet sees and treats a case of canker in an animal's ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' looks like the animal doctor; it is the verb, to check. 'case of' takes CR from canker.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet someone is to check them over, which is to screen them.

clue.text: Papers I notice left uncovered, that's foolish

parts.note: ID means identity papers

indicators.note: with its covering ends removed, only the middle of the word is left

explanation.surface: Someone notices that leaving their identity papers lying about was foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means very stupid, which is foolish.

clue.text: Survey of certain males in Turkey, say

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the other

parts.note: turkey is an example of meat
sure means certain
men are males

explanation.surface: A survey of particular men in the country of Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' looks like the country; it is the bird as food.
explanation.definitionFit: A survey of land measures it, so a measurement is a survey.
